tagline: Lafayette's towns, and a two-car ferry you call by horn.
intro: From Henderson the tour heads east on Warrenton Road into Warrenton, then out across farm country to Halifax on the Roanoke River and south to Scotland Neck. US 258 crosses the Roanoke to Rich Square, and back roads bring it to Murfreesboro on high ground above the Meherrin. A cable ferry takes the byway over that river, and the last miles run through Gatesville and east on US 158.
Lafayette came this way on his 1825 tour of the United States and spoke at Halifax on February 27. He is said to have stayed at a plantation south of Warrenton between his speeches.

moments.title: Warrenton
moments.text: Named for Joseph Warren of Bunker Hill, the town grew rich on tobacco and cotton in the years after Lafayette's visit, and many of its planters' houses still stand.

moments.title: Halifax
moments.text: The Fourth Provincial Congress met in this Roanoke River town and adopted the Halifax Resolves on April 12, 1776, and Lafayette came to speak here on February 27, 1825.

moments.title: Parker's Ferry
moments.text: The byway's way over the Meherrin is Parker's Ferry, a steel barge on a loose cable with room for two cars, which drivers waiting on the far bank have called over with the horn.

practical: The byway crosses the Meherrin on Parker's Ferry, which has room for two cars, does not run in high water or storms, and does not take recreational or larger vehicles. Check with NCDOT that it is operating before you go. The guidebook's alternate route runs by US 258 and US 158 to Winton.
